call_notes:
Rep: Tobias, good to hear from you. Did the signed paperwork make it over okay?

Tobias Parekh (Head of HR): So, honestly, we were leaning toward Corvane for a while. Everyone talks about them. But then the demo happened and I brought my list of questions, the ugly ones, like what happens when someone moves from our Texas office to Colorado mid-quarter. Tobias Parekh (Head of HR): Right. And the other thing, and this is a smaller thing, but your implementation lady, what's her name, Odile? She sent a week by week plan before we'd even signed. Who does what, what we need from Thaddeus by when, when we run payroll in parallel. Thaddeus, you printed it out, didn't you?
Thaddeus Galbraith (Payroll Manager): It's on my wall. Two parallel runs, then we cut over on the first pay period of the month. I can actually picture it.
Tobias Parekh (Head of HR): So that's it, really. The demo felt like it was built for us and the plan felt like a plan. We have sixty-seven people, three states, and I didn't want to be somebody's guinea pig.

Rep: Linnea, thanks for taking the time. I wanted to check in after the demo to see where things stand.
Linnea Galbraith (Office Manager): Of course. So, I'll be upfront. We've decided to go a different direction. We're making a change, but it's not with you, if that makes sense.

Linnea Galbraith (Office Manager): Oh, it's just where we landed. Honestly it was a good conversation all around. Rafferty and I went back and forth, and then we just made the call. The team was lovely, and I mean that.

Linnea Galbraith (Office Manager): No, no. Really. We just made a change. I wouldn't read anything into it.

Linnea Galbraith (Office Manager): We do, ha. We always do. Anyway, thank you for the demo. It was thorough, and the notes you sent were tidy.

Linnea Galbraith (Office Manager): Sure, that's fine. And please say thanks to your team from us.

call_notes:
Rep: Marisol, thank you for joining. I understand you have a decision to share.
Marisol Hollander (HR Generalist): Yes. I would like to be clear and fair to you. The platform itself performed well in the demonstration. Payroll, the multi-state filings, all of it was satisfactory.
Rep: I appreciate that. What was the deciding factor?
Marisol Hollander (HR Generalist): We hire constantly, and we need requisitions, candidate pipelines and offer letters in the same system as the employee record. You do not have an applicant tracking module. I asked about it twice in the demonstration, and the answer, quite properly, was that it is not offered. For us that is a requirement, not a preference.
Rep: Understood. Did you find something that does cover it?
Marisol Hollander (HR Generalist): We are looking at the options. I would add, in the interest of candour, that the project itself has also slowed. Our finance team imposed a freeze on new software spending until the new year. So even had the applicant tracking been present, I do not believe we could have signed this quarter.
Tobias Eastwood (Controller): That is correct. The freeze is a separate matter, though. The recruiting piece was the principal concern.
Rep: Thank you both. I will note that and keep you informed if we ever add it.
Marisol Hollander (HR Generalist): We would be grateful for that.

Rep: Beatrix, thanks for jumping on. How'd the numbers shake out?
Beatrix Petrakis (Operations Manager): Not great for you, I'm afraid. I'll just say it. Your quote comes to about eleven thousand a year for eighty-seven people. That's roughly a hundred and twenty-five a head. We found another option at under seven thousand. Close to eighty a head.
Rep: Okay. Is there anything on our side we could do on the structure? Fewer modules, a different term?
Beatrix Petrakis (Operations Manager): I asked Fenella the same thing. Fenella?
Fenella Hollander (General Manager): We looked at it. Even stripped down, you were still four grand over what we budgeted. Staffing margins are thin. I can't carry that. I liked the product, I'm not going to pretend otherwise. But I run a tight ship and the cheaper one does what we need.
Beatrix Petrakis (Operations Manager): The demo was fine. Your people were responsive. It's just a number.
Rep: I hear you. Appreciate you being direct.
Beatrix Petrakis (Operations Manager): Easier that way. We've got a payroll run Friday and I'd rather not spend all week chasing this.
Rep: Understood. If your budget changes, I'm around.
Beatrix Petrakis (Operations Manager): Will do.

Rep: Beatrix, thank you for making time. I wanted to understand where things stand.
Beatrix Whitlock (Office Manager): Certainly. I will be straightforward with you, and I hope you will not take it badly. We have started with another provider.
Rep: I appreciate you telling me. May I ask what happened?
Beatrix Whitlock (Office Manager): It is largely a matter of timing. We first spoke on a Tuesday in the spring. We asked for a demonstration, and the first slot that could be offered was nineteen days later. Nineteen days. In that interval our director, Fenella, became rather impatient. She had been promised something for the board meeting, and she could not wait.
Fenella Whitlock (Operations Director): That is accurate. I told Beatrix that I could not present a plan without a system at least in motion. So we began a trial with someone else the following week. By the time your demonstration took place, we had already loaded half our employee records elsewhere.
Beatrix Whitlock (Office Manager): And I will say the demonstration was good. It simply arrived after our momentum had gone. We were no longer in the mood to compare.
Rep: I understand. I am sorry we were not faster.
Beatrix Whitlock (Office Manager): It is no one's fault in particular. Calendars are what they are. But a week or so, I think, we could have managed.
Rep: Thank you for the candour. I will take that back to the team.
Beatrix Whitlock (Office Manager): You are very welcome.

Rep: Mirela, congratulations on getting everyone aligned. I gather it took a while.
Mirela Okonkwo (People Operations Lead): It did, and I apologise for the long gap between our first conversation and the demonstration. We had a reorganisation, and then the holidays. I appreciate your patience.
Rep: Not at all. What helped you decide?
Mirela Okonkwo (People Operations Lead): Two things, principally. The demonstration answered the questions I had written down in advance. I had eleven. I wanted to know how a correction to a prior pay period is handled, how a late timesheet is reflected, who can see salary data. Each one was addressed in turn without any evasion. I ticked them off as we went.
Fenella Nakamura (General Manager): I will add something. I was sceptical, as I am with all software. But your support person, when we sent a question over the weekend before signing, replied within the hour. On a Sunday. That told me what the relationship would be like.
Mirela Okonkwo (People Operations Lead): Yes. That was Fenella's deciding point, I believe. We are a small team, sixty-one people on one site, and we cannot afford to wait for a ticket.
Rep: I am glad. Our implementation lead will send the schedule on Monday.
Mirela Okonkwo (People Operations Lead): Splendid. We are looking forward to it.
Fenella Nakamura (General Manager): As are we.

Rep: Casper, thanks for the call. I heard there was news.

Casper Hollander (Operations Manager): Our broker. He's handled our benefits renewals for, what, eleven years? When he says this is the package for a company our size, I listen. He put the bundle in front of us, payroll and enrollment and renewal reporting together, and said it'd be one less thing for him to chase every October.
Rep: Did he compare it to what we showed you?
Casper Hollander (Operations Manager): He didn't need to. I trust him. Your demo was solid, I'll tell you that, I took four pages of notes. But he is the one who is on the phone with me when the carrier changes terms. Casper, you want to add anything?
Casper Jessamy (Controller): Just that it's the broker relationship. Nothing against you.
Rep: Understood. I'd rather you're well served.
Casper Hollander (Operations Manager): Appreciate it.
closing_email:
Subject: Our decision

Hi,

Please know the demo was thorough and we appreciated how quickly you answered our follow-up questions.

Best regards,
Casper Hollander
Thornfield Fabrication

Oriel Thorsen (COO): The price was a bit more than we had pencilled in, I will mention, but that was not the reason. It is a matter of the calendar.
Rep: Understood. Would it be useful if I checked back in the new year?
Yuki Abernethy (Office Manager): That would be welcome. Perhaps late January.

closing_email:

Your Lanternmere HR team

Rafferty Moreau (VP of People): Sure. Always. Send a note around the holidays. Or whenever.

Rafferty Moreau (VP of People): No. We're all set.
Maren Santangelo (Compliance Lead): Thanks for all the time you put in, and for putting up with our questions.

Rafferty Moreau (VP of People): Nothing big. Hiking, if the rain stops. My kid has a soccer thing.

Rafferty Moreau (VP of People): Likewise. Take care of yourself. Say hi to the team.

Rafferty Moreau (VP of People): You too. Bye now.
Maren Santangelo (Compliance Lead): Bye.

Teodoro Ivarsson (COO): So, I'm sorry, I know you've put time into this, and I wanted to tell you in person rather than let it go quiet. We're pausing. Everything. Not just you.

Teodoro Ivarsson (COO): Well, so, you know we're a dental group, a hundred and seven people across four states, and the owners have been in talks about buying a practice in the next county, and as of last Thursday that has eaten every spare dollar. Our managing partner basically said no new software, no new anything until the acquisition is settled. Which could be spring, could be summer, who knows.
Bram Santangelo (HR Director): And honestly I was the champion on this. I loved the demo. I'd already drawn up a rough timeline in my head, like, we cut over right after the first of the year, and now I'm just, ugh.
Rep: So you haven't gone with anyone else?
Bram Santangelo (HR Director): No, no, nobody. We're staying on the spreadsheets and the old payroll service. Which, I know.
Teodoro Ivarsson (COO): Please don't read it as anything about what you showed us. The numbers were fine, the product was fine, my people liked it. It's just the timing from above. Like a door closing in the next room.
Rep: Could I check back in a couple of months?
Teodoro Ivarsson (COO): Please do. Bram will text you if it opens up sooner.
closing_email:
Subject: Pausing our HR platform project

Hi,

Thanks again for the time you and your team gave us over the past few weeks. I wanted to follow our call with something in writing. The group has put all new spending on hold while the owners work through a possible acquisition, so we are not moving ahead with any new HR or payroll system for now. We haven't chosen another vendor. This has nothing to do with the demo or the proposal, which Bram and I both thought were strong. We'll reach out as soon as we have a clearer picture, likely sometime after the new year. Please keep us on your list.

Best,
Teodoro

call_notes:
Noor Vasquez (Chief People Officer): Let me give you the short version of what moved us, and Odalys can correct me. Three days. That's the gap between our first call and the demo, and I'd marked it down: the spreadsheet I keep on vendors had you at three days, and the other outfit our broker sent us, Tallyhold, at nineteen. Not a scientific measure, but it told me who was paying attention.
Rep: I appreciate you tracking that.
Noor Vasquez (Chief People Officer): In the demo itself, I'd sent you four questions beforehand. One, can we run weekly pay for shop floor and biweekly for salaried staff in the same cycle. Two, how do overtime rules differ when we cross from our Ohio plant to the Indiana one. Three, onboarding for about thirty seasonal hires. Four, what the audit trail looks like. All four got answered on screen, not promised in a follow-up.
Odalys Lindgren (CFO): I came in on the second call and I'll say I was the difficult one. I asked about the total cost over three years, including implementation, since a hundred and seventy-nine employees with seasonal swings means headcount will fluctuate, and I asked what happens to the per-employee fee when we drop to a hundred and fifty in the slow quarter.
Rep: And what did you hear?
Odalys Lindgren (CFO): That it flexes monthly on active employees, in writing, which I then had my controller read. I asked about the data migration risk, and instead of reassuring me you showed me the cutover plan, six weeks, with named owners and a parallel run on the first payroll. That's what I wanted. Dates and names.
Noor Vasquez (Chief People Officer): She went from arms crossed to forwarding me the order form.
Odalys Lindgren (CFO): I'll have a few more questions on the invoicing schedule, but yes. We're going ahead. The plan was concrete, and the demo wasn't a slide show.
Rep: Thank you both. I'll get kickoff dates to you this week.
closing_email:
Subject: Moving forward with Lanternmere HR

Hi,

Please take this as our go-ahead. Odalys has signed off after reviewing the monthly headcount flexing and the six-week cutover plan, which answered what she needed. For me, the deciding factors were the speed of the demo after our first call (three days) and that every question I sent ahead was answered live. Can you send over the order form and propose two kickoff windows in the first half of next month? Our controller will want a copy of the plan too.

Thanks,
Noor

call_notes:
Fenella Nakamura (Operations Manager): For the record, here's what I'd say to anyone asking. First call to demo was five days. We had a Corvane quote sitting on my desk the whole time, and honestly if you'd taken two weeks I'd have just signed theirs to get it off my plate.
Rep: Glad we got there in time.
Fenella Nakamura (Operations Manager): The demo covered the three things I'd actually written down: how we'd handle our two states' filings, how an employee changes their direct deposit without calling me, and how long implementation would take. You didn't wander.
Signe Ashgrove (CFO): My turn. I asked pointed questions, I know. I wanted the payroll tax filing liability in writing, who carries the penalty if a filing is late, and the exit terms if we leave after year one. Your colleague didn't flinch. We went through the contract clause by clause, and the penalty language was clearer than I expected.
Fenella Nakamura (Operations Manager): She had a page and a half of questions.
Signe Ashgrove (CFO): Two pages, actually. Every one got a straight answer. The implementation plan, eight weeks, with a weekly check-in, helped. I was ready to be a no and I'm a yes.
Rep: That's great to hear.
Fenella Nakamura (Operations Manager): So, send the paperwork. We'd like to start before the quarter ends.

Oriel Rourke (Head of HR): Quick summary of how we got here, for your notes. Our first call was on the ninth, the demo on the fourteenth. Five days. I liked that, because I had told my leadership team I'd bring a recommendation in three weeks, and a slow vendor would have eaten the schedule.
Rep: That timeline was tight. Thanks for being clear about it.
Oriel Rourke (Head of HR): In the demo, I'd asked to see what an employee in one of our five states gets when they log in on day one, and what a manager sees when approving time off. You showed both. Nothing mocked up. I also asked who answers when payroll is wrong at eleven at night, and you showed me the support queue and told me the actual average response time. Under an hour, was it?

Oriel Rourke (Head of HR): Right, and I took that back to Signe.
Signe Vasquez (CFO): I did my homework. I read the contract before the call and I had eleven questions. I tend to trust people who put numbers on paper.
Oriel Rourke (Head of HR): She went from skeptical to asking when we can start.
Signe Vasquez (CFO): The implementation timeline convinced me. Seven weeks, owners named. Let's do it.
closing_email:
Subject: Welcome aboard, Quarry Design Studio

call_notes:

Which works out to around nineteen dollars a head per month, right?

Marisol Dunmore (VP of People): Right. And Tallyhold came back at, I think, twelve a head. So about nineteen thousand a year. That's eleven thousand dollars of difference, and, I mean, I could hire a part-timer for that. Almost.

I'm the one who signs off on the budget, and this year we've got the new press line going in at the plant, which is not cheap, and I told Marisol I just can't stretch to thirty. Rafferty Petrakis (General Manager): I appreciate it but it's still going to be above where I need to be. Let's say we go with the cheaper one, and revisit later.
closing_email:
Subject: Our decision

call_notes:
Thaddeus Thorsen (People Operations Lead): I'll give you the timeline, because I think the timeline is the story. Our inbound request went in on the third. We had the intro call on the fourth. The demo was on the ninth. That's five days between the call and the demo, five by my count, and in the meantime I had a standing meeting with Annelise on the Thursday where I told her we'd have something to show.
Rep: And on that Thursday, what happened?
Thaddeus Thorsen (People Operations Lead): I had nothing to show. So I did what I'd do, I took the Brasswick trial that we'd been offered earlier, because it was available that afternoon, and I started loading people into it. Forty-one employees by Friday evening, which I'm a little embarrassed to say.
Annelise Oyelaran (HR Director): I'll add the other side. When Thaddeus said the demo was Monday, I said, fine, but I've got a decision window. Our current provider's contract auto-renews on the thirtieth, and I needed to know by the twentieth whether we were replacing it. With the Brasswick trial, I could see a real roster. With the demo, I had an hour of sample data, and I'm sorry, I mean that kindly.
Rep: The demo wasn't a bad fit, though?
Thaddeus Thorsen (People Operations Lead): It was good. I'd say seven out of ten on my scorecard, but by then Brasswick was at eight because it already had my data in it. I couldn't justify tearing up a trial that was a quarter loaded to start rollout planning for a different product. It's inertia, it's not a judgement on you.
Annelise Oyelaran (HR Director): Momentum matters in a project like this. We lost ours waiting, and the other vendor happened to be there.
Rep: Understood. I appreciate the candor.
Thaddeus Thorsen (People Operations Lead): If it helps, shorten that gap for the next person.
closing_email:
Subject: Update on our evaluation

Hi,

Thanks for the demo last week. I wanted to let you know that we've started implementing with another provider. The five days between our first call and the demo gave us time to begin a trial elsewhere, and we're now too far along to switch. It wasn't about the product. Feel free to check in next year.

Thaddeus

call_notes:

call_notes:
Linnea Ashgrove (HR Generalist): Short version. We're going with you.

Linnea Ashgrove (HR Generalist): And you did. I wrote my questions down on the first call. Scheduling for the vet techs, who work odd shifts. Payroll for people who work at two clinics. Tips and bonuses. Four states. You showed me every one of them. Not a deck. The real system.
Beatrix Moreau (Head of People): I was on the second part. I run the day-to-day. I'm the one who'd have to train eighty-odd clinic managers and techs. I asked how long that takes. You said two sessions, an hour each. Then you showed me the training plan. It was a page. Clear.

Beatrix Moreau (Head of People): It's what I needed. I've done migrations. They go bad when nobody knows who does what. Your plan said who does what.
Linnea Ashgrove (HR Generalist): Same for me. I'm one person doing HR for a hundred and eighty people. I can't take on a mess. You made it feel doable.
Beatrix Moreau (Head of People): Dates matter to me. You gave us dates. Go-live on the first pay period of next month. Parallel run before that.

Linnea Ashgrove (HR Generalist): Good. Hold yourselves. We'll hold you.
Beatrix Moreau (Head of People): Send the order form today. Please.
Linnea Ashgrove (HR Generalist): And thank you. Seriously. That wasn't a normal sales process.

Our CEO left. The interim CEO froze discretionary spending through at least the second quarter. And the board asked me to hold all system projects that touch more than ten percent of staff, which payroll obviously does.
Rep: That's a lot to absorb. Does the freeze apply across the board?
Emeka Lindgren (Director of Operations): Everything over five thousand dollars. Your contract is, I believe, in the low thirties, so it's well past the line. And there's no one to appeal to until the permanent hire is made, which the board estimates at four to six months.
Bastian Abernethy (Benefits Manager): For what it's worth, I have the list I made after your demo. Nine requirements, and you met eight of them cleanly. I don't have a complaint. I actually argued for you in the internal review.
Rep: I appreciate that. You haven't engaged anyone else?
Emeka Lindgren (Director of Operations): No. We're 152 employees across five states and we're staying with what we have. It's inefficient, but it's funded.
Bastian Abernethy (Benefits Manager): I'd just ask that you not forget us. If the freeze lifts in the spring, we'd pick this up where we left off.
Rep: I'll keep your materials ready.
closing_email:

call_notes:
Amara Petrakis (VP of People): So Ravi and I have been chewing on this for days, and, okay, Ravi, you tell it, because it's really your thing.

We have four carriers, medical, dental, vision, and a life one, and each one wants a file from us in their own format, like their own spreadsheet layout, uploaded to their own portal. When I asked in the demo, hey, does Lanternmere send those files to the carriers automatically, the answer was, you can export a report and upload it yourself.
Rep: Yes, that's accurate today.
Ravi Vasquez (Benefits Manager): And that's the part I can't get past. I mean, the rest of it, super nice. The employee screens are lovely. But I'd still be doing the copy-machine thing. Four carriers, a hundred and twenty-nine people, every change, every new hire, every life event.
Amara Petrakis (VP of People): And we asked, is it coming? And I appreciated that nobody made something up. But a maybe next year doesn't help us in November.
Ravi Vasquez (Benefits Manager): Tax stuff was fine, by the way. Cost was fine. Just the feeds.
Amara Petrakis (VP of People): It really is just that one thing. Ravi would quit. I'm kidding. Mostly.

Priya Petrakis (HR Generalist): I'll be straight with you. We're going with Tallyhold.
Rep: I appreciate you telling me. Can you share what drove it?
Priya Petrakis (HR Generalist): Our broker. We've used her for six years. She handles our renewals, she negotiates with the carriers, she knows our people. When she says look at this one, I look at it.
Rep: Did she explain why Tallyhold?
Priya Petrakis (HR Generalist): She put a bundle in front of us. Payroll, benefits admin, the whole thing, one invoice. She said it fits a company our size. A hundred and two people. I trust her.
Wren Castellane (COO): I should say something. I came in late. I'm the one who asked why we'd change a relationship that works. Our broker has saved us money on every renewal. She picks up the phone on Sunday. When she brings us a package, I'm not going to second-guess her to save a few hours of comparison.
Rep: That makes sense. Was there anything in the product that gave you pause?
Priya Petrakis (HR Generalist): No. Honestly. Your demo was good. I liked the time-off screens. I told my sister about them, she runs HR at a bakery chain, and she was jealous.
Wren Castellane (COO): It's not about the product. It's about who's on our side. Our broker is.
Priya Petrakis (HR Generalist): And it's one less thing to manage. She said she'd handle the setup with them. That's a big deal for me because I'm also the office manager half the time. Last week I fixed a printer and a payroll error before lunch.
Wren Castellane (COO): Which is exactly why we shouldn't be adding projects to her plate.
Rep: Is there anything I could do to change the picture?
Priya Petrakis (HR Generalist): No. Don't take it personally. If our broker changes her recommendation someday, I'll call you.
Wren Castellane (COO): We'll keep your number.
Rep: Thanks for the candor, both of you.
closing_email:
Subject: Thank you, and staying in touch

Hi Priya,

Thank you for letting me know where you landed. I understand that the bundle your broker put together made this an easy call, and that trust is worth a great deal. I enjoyed working with you and Wren, and I'm glad the time-off screens landed well. If your renewal conversation ever reopens the question of payroll, I would welcome the chance to be considered. In the meantime, I'll leave you alone, and wish you a smooth setup.

Best,
Your Lanternmere HR rep

call_notes:

Bastian Parekh (HR Director): No. Yours was live, and I threw my ugliest scenario at you, the one with a part-time driver who goes full-time mid-pay-period and moves from Georgia to Tennessee. And you just did it. I watched it get done.

Ingrid Zeller (Finance Director): Specific answers. A named person for the first three payrolls. A commitment to correct filing errors at your cost. I asked for it in the contract and it was there the next day. So, fine. I'm supportive. Don't make it weird.
Bastian Parekh (HR Director): She's supportive. Write that down.

closing_email:

Bastian

call_notes:

And whether the system would let us run a payroll off-cycle when a seasonal canning-line hire starts on a Wednesday. You answered each one live, in the product, without going to find someone.
Soren Ashgrove (IT Manager): My piece was identity and access. I asked about single sign-on, about how accounts are deprovisioned when someone leaves, and about the data export format in case we ever leave. You pulled up the admin settings and walked through them. I don't say this often, but it didn't feel like a sales call.
Signe Cadogan (Chief People Officer): And the demo was five days after we first spoke, which matters to me, because I'd raised it with the owners the same week and they were still paying attention. With 121 employees, we don't have a procurement department.

Soren Ashgrove (IT Manager): Clear. Six weeks, with my part limited to about eight hours total. I counted.

Signe Zeller (Payroll Manager): I can confirm that. I was told yesterday that every open initiative is on hold until the structure is settled. Our current system will simply continue.
Rep: Have you spoken with any other provider?
Lucian Santangelo (VP of People): No. None. We have not engaged anyone. I should like to be clear that your demonstration and your proposal were both excellent, and the figures were within what we had expected.
Signe Zeller (Payroll Manager): Nothing about the product was at issue.

Hollis Ashgrove (Head of HR): Correct. The difficulty is not the product. It is the sum on the invoice.

Rep: Thank you both. I appreciate the directness.

Kwame Fonseca (People Operations Lead): First. We have virtual instructors who live in states where we have no campus. At what point is a registration with the state required, and does your service open the account, or do we? Second. Several employees work in Kentucky, where there are local occupational license taxes assessed by county and city. Does the system calculate and remit those?

Kofi Fonseca (Head of Finance): May I add a third? Our teachers are paid over twelve months on ten-month contracts. In June and July, a number of them relocate out of state. In those cases, which state receives the withholding for those months, and is the year-end reporting split correctly?

Kofi Fonseca (Head of Finance): I will be candid. Your pricing is acceptable. It sits slightly above our budget and we could have accommodated it. The difficulty is that each of these questions has resulted in a follow-up, and with twelve states, we cannot afford a vendor who is uncertain.

Rep: Please. I would appreciate that.

Before it, we had sent you a list of eleven questions, concerning our commission payments and how we handle our freelancers who convert to staff. You answered them in order, using our own sample records. I had been told by two other vendors that this sort of thing could be discussed after signing. You simply showed us.
Sunniva Jessamy (HR Director): For my part, I would point to the implementation plan. You gave us a written schedule with weekly milestones, who on your side would be responsible, and who on ours. We have 248 employees in seven states, and a poorly planned migration could cost us a payroll cycle. Your plan reassured me more than any feature.

Sunniva Jessamy (HR Director): Please send the agreement to both of us. We would like to hold the kickoff the week after we sign.
Wren Ivarsson (Director of Operations): And please do introduce us to the person who will lead our implementation. I would prefer to know them before the first day.
Rep: Certainly. I will arrange that by Monday.
Sunniva Jessamy (HR Director): Thank you. We look forward to it.

Ravi Quillfeather (Office Manager): So it's been eighteen days. From the first call to the demo. Eighteen. I counted this morning, I even looked back at my calendar. Sunniva Ibarra (General Manager): I did say that. I'm not proud of the tone, but I did.
Ravi Quillfeather (Office Manager): So we signed up with somebody else. A smaller outfit, they called back the same day, and they were up and running before you and I even got on this call. Sunniva Ibarra (General Manager): If it helps, I'd say, set the demo faster. People get restless.
Ravi Quillfeather (Office Manager): Yeah, that, definitely. Anyway, we'll keep your number. Good luck out there!

Rep: Annelise, Idris, thanks for joining. Let's talk about where things stand.
Annelise Petrakis (COO): Yes. I'll be as precise as I can. We are an 84-person company in one state. We've been with our benefits broker for nine years, and she renews our medical, dental, vision, our 401(k) plan, and our workers' comp. When we told her we were looking at payroll and HR systems, she came back within a week with a recommendation: Tallyhold. It came as a bundle, benefits administration and payroll under one contract, and she negotiated the renewal terms alongside it.
Rep: Understood. Did you compare it against what we showed you?
Annelise Petrakis (COO): Somewhat. Your demo was well organized. I counted eleven features I liked. But when I put the two side by side, I found the gap was small. Two or three points either way. What tipped it was this: our broker is the person who calls when an enrollment fails, or a claim is denied. She is in the middle of the relationship already. Moving payroll to a different vendor means she is no longer in the loop for that part, and I don't wish to have two escalation paths.
Idris Oyelaran (COO): I'll add that I asked her directly whether she was receiving anything for the recommendation. She said she is compensated by the carriers, not the software, and I believed her. She has never steered us wrong. When the bundle came from her, I was inclined to trust it.
Rep: Is there anything in our offering that would change your thinking?
Annelise Petrakis (COO): Honestly, no. It is not a criticism of your product. The broker put the bundle in front of us, and it reduces our administrative burden.
Idris Oyelaran (COO): We did the arithmetic, and it came out about even.
Rep: I appreciate your candor. If circumstances change, please call.
Annelise Petrakis (COO): We will. Thank you for your thoroughness.
